ees a compact digest, and a read-only sidebar tab mirrors it.
# dsh-checklists

Session-scoped checklists for **DeepSeek Harness**. The agent owns the list, the
model always sees i
t, and a read-only sidebar tab mirrors it.

The problem this solves is not "having a list". It is having to **dictate the list
again** every ses

sion. Here the checklist is created once, injected into the model
context on every turn, and updated
as work progresses — no reminders needed.
## How it works

1. The agent creates a checklist (`checklist_create`), optionally from a template.
2. A compact dige

st of every checklist is injected into the prompt on each
assembly, so the model always knows what i

s pending.
3. The agent marks items as it finishes them (`checklist_check`).
4. The sidebar tab show
s the same tree, read-only, updated every two seconds.
If the agent forgets to mark something, you say so in chat and it fixes it.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `checklist_create` | Creates a list, from scratch or from a template (`release`, `feature`, `debug

`, `review`) |
| `checklist_add` | Appends items to an existing list, optionally under a given item

|
| `checklist_check` | Sets one or more items to `todo` · `doing` · `done` · `blocked` |
| `checkli

st_next` | Returns the next actionable leaf, its path, and how many remain |
| `checklist_edit` | Ch

anges an item's text (not its state) |
| `checklist_list` | Full tree with ids and states, for when

the digest is truncated |
| `checklist_delete` | Deletes a list (by id or exact title) |
| `checklis

t_remove_item` | Removes one item and everything nested under it |
| `checklist_rename` | Renames a

list; titles stay unique within the session |
| `checklist_workspace` | Lists checklists from other

sessions in the same workspace (read-only) |
| `checklist_template_save` | Saves a list as a reusabl
e template for future sessions |
Items are plain strings. **Two leading spaces per level** nest them:

## Data
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Writes are atomic (temp file + rename) and serialized per session. A corrupt
document degrades to an
empty list instead of failing the turn.

> The package is `dsh-checklists`, but its storage directory keeps the
> `dsh-checklist` prefix. Tha

t path is data, not identity: renaming it would orphan
> every checklist already saved.
## Sidebar tab
Open the right sidebar, then the **guide** (`+`) and pick **Checklist**.
| Action | How |

| Collapse | Click a list title, or the `▾` on any item with children |
| Auto-collapse | When a **n

ew** list appears, the others fold and the new one opens |
| Hide completed | The "Hide done" button

, shown only when something is done |
| Copy as markdown | "Copy" — paste into a PR or an issue |
|
Edit an item's text | **Double-click** the text; Enter saves, Esc cancels |

Item **states** remain agent-only: the tab cannot check anything off. The one write
path is text edi

ting, through `POST /dsh-checklist/item` with `expectedText`. If the
item changed since the tab read

it, the host answers **409** rather than overwriting
the agent's edit.
## HTTP routes
| Route | Method | Purpose |

| `/dsh-checklist/state` | GET | One session's state (read-only, `no-store`) |
| `/dsh-checklist/ite

m` | POST | Edit an item's text, with a conflict guard |
| `/dsh-checklist/nudge` | GET | Recent tur

n-end gate decisions |
| `/dsh-checklist/workspace` | GET | Checklists of sibling sessions in the sa

me workspace |
| `/dsh-checklist/client-probe` | GET | Client load diagnostics |
## Turn-end gate

A checklist only helps while it is true. The gate closes the most common gap:
a turn does real work,

forgets to mark it, and the list is stale by the time you
look at it.
When a turn is about to close, the plugin checks exactly three things:

1. Did the turn run a tool that changes the workspace (`bash`, `edit`, `write`, …)?
2. Did it skip e

very checklist write?
3. Is anything still marked `doing`?
If all three hold, the agent gets one short steering message before the turn ends:

> Before you finish: N checklist item(s) are still marked "doing". If you
> completed any of them th

is turn, update them with checklist_check and say what
> proves it. If not, leave them as they are —
do not mark work you did not do.

It never guesses **what** was completed — only that the bookkeeping was skipped.
At most one nudge p

er turn, and none when the turn was pure conversation or the
checklist already changed.
Inspect recent decisions at `GET /dsh-checklist/nudge`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`nudge: observe` records without interrupting; `nudge: off` disables the gate.
## Workspace lens

Checklists stay per session. The lens is a **read-only** way to see the
checklists of other sessions

in the same project — available on request, and
never part of the prompt.
| Mode | Behaviour |

| `on-demand` (default) | The tool works; the sidebar section starts collapsed |
| `always` | The si

debar section starts expanded |
| `off` | No tool, no route |

Clicking an entry expands it into a read-only tree, fetched once from that
session's own state route

. Nothing there is editable — the lens can look, not
touch.

Membership comes from disk: a session belongs to the workspace directory that
contains it under `$DS

H_HOME/sessions/<workspace>/<sessionId>/`. The host's
`workspace.json` is only used for a friendly t

itle, because it is not always
complete — on the machine this was written on it was missing a worksp

, because it is not always
complete — on the machine this was written on it was missing a workspace.

Nothing here is writable. To change another session's checklist, open that
session: two writers on o
ne list would give the list two truths.
